replication.target_description: Autobiographical Concealed Information Test: conceal versus reveal motivation, high versus low item salience, and SCR/RLL/HR responses. Assigned description and p.5 do not identify a unique ANOVA main effect, interaction, or planned contrast.

n.sample_role: Participants; candidate measure-specific analytic counts only, not assigned to a unique target test.
n.exclusions: Skin conductance and HR lost for one participant; respiration lost for one additional participant; SCR removed for seven participants and HR for one; additional block-level SCR nonresponsivity and individual-response movement/outlier exclusions. No critical-model N derived from df.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied cache contains UvA-DARE cover identifying final published version, title Unraveling the roles of orienting and inhibition in the Concealed Information Test, klein Selle / Verschuere / Kindt / Meijer / Ben-Shakhar, 2017, Psychophysiology 54, 628–639, DOI 10.1111/psyp.12825; matching article title, authors and DOI appear in article header. Full report includes methods, results, discussion, appendices and references; accepted as matching primary replication report, rather than abstract-only parse. No PDF supplied; no PDF rendered. Original and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not assessments. No unique target can be selected from the broad description and p.5 locator (article p.632). Candidate same-test pairs on p.632: motivational-condition main effect F(1,98)=84.34, Cohen’s ƒ=.93, p<.001; item-salience main effect F(1,98)=4.81, ƒ=.22, p=.031; physiological-measure main effect F(2,196)=77.46, ƒ=.89, p<.001; physiological measure × motivational condition F(2,196)=17.10, ƒ=.42, p<.001; physiological measure × item salience F(2,196)=5.96, ƒ=.25, p=.003. Further candidate planned contrasts on p.633: motivational-condition contrast ƒ=.40, p<.001; salience contrast ƒ=.18, p=.001. Cohen’s ƒ is explicitly named in Data Analysis on p.632. Canonical OCR prints the first contrast t as 24.98; not repaired without PDF. No candidate selected by magnitude or row order. Candidate participant counts: recruited 109, allocated 55 conceal and 54 reveal (p.630); measure-specific nSCR=101, nRLL=108, nHR=107 (p.632). These counts do not explicitly establish the complete-case three-measure ANOVA sample. At least 100 is a lower bound, not exact analytic N. No N inferred from df; no analytic N sums performed. Table 3, p.634 gives additional measure/condition counts but no unique assigned test mapping. Retain all candidates for parent field-scope review.
